title: Census of India 2027 Overview
tagline: Your intelligent civic companion for Census 2027
whatIsCensus: The Census of India is the largest administrative and statistical exercise in the world. Conducted under the Census Act, 1948, it counts every resident in India and gathers vital social, economic, and demographic data that shapes national policy, electoral delimitation, resource distribution, and infrastructure planning.

whyItMatters.title: Policy & Resource Allocation
whyItMatters.description: Government schemes, healthcare facilities, schools, roads, and subsidies are planned using granular Census data at village, town, and district levels.

whyItMatters.title: Electoral Representation
whyItMatters.description: Delimitation and allocation of parliamentary and legislative constituencies are anchored in Census population figures.

whyItMatters.title: Inclusive Development
whyItMatters.description: Helps identify underserved communities, demographic shifts, literacy gaps, and migration patterns to deliver targeted welfare.

digitalCensus2027Innovations.title: Digital Self-Enumeration
digitalCensus2027Innovations.description: For the first time in Indian Census history, citizens will have the option to fill out Census questionnaires online for their household before field enumerators visit.

digitalCensus2027Innovations.title: Mobile App Field Enumeration
digitalCensus2027Innovations.description: Enumerators will collect and upload household responses directly through secured, government-authorized mobile applications, eliminating paper delays.

digitalCensus2027Innovations.title: Census Management & Monitoring Portal (CMMS)
digitalCensus2027Innovations.description: Real-time tracking of enumeration coverage, geo-referencing, and data validation across all 36 States and Union Territories.

legalFramework.confidentialitySection: Section 15 of the Census Act guarantees that all individual census records are strictly confidential and cannot be produced as evidence in any court of law or accessed by tax, police, or investigative authorities.
legalFramework.distinctionFromOtherRegisters: The Census is a statistical demographic count of all persons residing in India at the time of enumeration. It is distinct from citizen registries, and participation is a civic duty protected by statutory confidentiality.

officialAuthority: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (ORGI), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
